He chuckles. "Not devilry, just Revachol's best topping pie!"
He clears his throat and continues. "That's actually peas, nothing, no amount of corporate espionage would ever would ever put them *so far* ahead of everyone else..."
He leans in so close you can feel his lukewarm breath against your jaw. "Just do your part as an officer of the RCM."
He looks around, half-ashamed, half-relieved.
He nods gravely. "I've been tempted on occasion. But someone has to stay strong for Revachol." His gaze shifts to the pile of soggy logs at his feet.
He pouts. "Most people don't... until it's too late. You have been warned. Do with this warning what you will."
He sighs again, hangs his head, and unbuttons his shirt fully. A cuirass that matches the dead man's boots comes into view. Soon it is in your hands -- smelling of his sweat.
He sighs. "Okay, fine, you got me. I'm a special *topping pie* delivery courier."
He smiles broadly.
He turns toward Kim. "I mean... *officers*."
His companion sighs. "Another trip to the reeds..."

The cryptozoologist's companion says nothing but nods approvingly in your direction.
The man forces out an unpleasant and artificial laugh. "C'mon, officer, you *know* that's not it. No way!"
The man simply nods, his long blond hair falling on his shoulders.
"*Cryptids*, actually. It's a so-called 'colonial animal', presenting as a large singular body, when in actuality, it's a congregation of tiny organisms working in unison."

"*Exactly*, officer." He leans in closer. "The Seolites are helping themselves from the future. And every little incremental improvement they receive in the present has *major* ripples all along the timeline..."
"... and attack it over and over again, you could theoretically punch your way back to the Franconigerian era!"
"... by about 4.5 seconds."
"...and use their superior technology to blackmail, mislead, and manipulate, turning high-ranking people in government and corporations into Seolite agents."
"A rhinoceros that looks ordinary during the day, but burns brightly by night. Well, at least the males do."
"Absolutely!" He nods enthusiastically, shooting a quick glance at the lieutenant. "That definitely *helps*, but that alone? I don't buy it..."
"Ahm..." He's so surprised he even forgets to close his mouth. "That's... yes, that's also horrible. I mean in a much grander scale. Exactly what happened to that village."
"All right. Of course, officer."
"Always a pleasure to see an officer of the law!"
"And I realize that their hygiene habits were completely appropriate for a nascent culture... I just didn't feel comfortable. Let's change the topic."

"And I'll *never* do it again. I don't know what got into me, really... work has been stressful lately. Damn Kojkos price dumping us out of competition."
"And keep an eye on that partner of yours." He lets the silence linger, then concludes: "Good talk."
"And personally, it seems easier than accessing deep-secret Seolite technology and more civilised than digital castigation, but to each his own."
"And personally, it seems easier than, say, accessing deep-secret Seolite technology, but to each his own."
"And personally, it seems more civilised than, say, digital castigation, but to each his own."
"And speaking personally, arranging an expedition seems like the most promising option overall, so I'm not really sure what else to tell you..."

"And then you hear rumours..." He flashes a quick side-glance at the lieutenant. "... that the Seolites possess technology that actually lets them move through time like it's a corridor. Back and forth, you see."

"As I explained, they count up to 12 on their fingers, but they divide the day into 15 parts. But that's a whole other discussion..."
"Assuming you survive the encounter... But that's way down the line of course..."

"Believe me, it's there. Technology so advanced it defies description..." He's avoiding your gaze.

"But everything's so... moist."

"But then, there are rumours going around that the Seolites have developed a technology that allows them to move through time like it's a corridor. Back and forth, you see."

"But... why were you in my apartment, officer?"
"By removing one segment from their fingers, they remove the corresponding hour from their life -- that's what they believe, anyway."
"COME ON, MORELL. WE'VE BEEN SOAKING OUT HERE FOR DAYS. IT'S TIME TO GO BACK."
"COME ON, SHE WANTS US BACK. I'M SOAKED UP TO MY NUTS OVER HERE. WE'LL BOTH CATCH REED CRABS IF WE DON'T DRY OUT SOON."
"Come on, officer, everybody knows about it." He rubs the back of his head, looking down. "The stuff they've got, most people here can't even *dream* of it..."
"Consider, though: Seol is famous, or shall I say, infamous, for its spy tech. Don't you find it... convenient?"
"Could be, could easily be." He nods enthusiastically, shooting a quick glance at the lieutenant. "I mean it definitely *helps*, but the market alone? I don't buy it..."
"DID HE SAY WE CAN GO BACK NOW?"
"Dark times will do that to good men." He nods gravely, then shifts his gaze to the floor tiles.

"Do I know how to turn back time...?" He gives you a sideways glance. "Is that a trick question?"

"During the Burning Rhino's mating season, herds of male rhinos, all aflame, encircle herds of female rhinos, forming a fiery ring as they begin to copulate, loudly."
"Enjoy." He smiles broadly.
"Essentially it's a grief ritual practiced by some old kipt tribes. Traditionally, after the death of a village leader, the bereaved are supposed to cut off a segment of their own fingers..."
"Even as Seol remains closed off from the world, Seolite agents have been slowly advancing through the echelons of power on the other isolae."
"Everyone was picking those pieces off him and I was watching them do it. And they scattered his clothes all over the yard, everything was smelling..." He looks at his feet.

"Exactly! That's exactly what it was -- civic duty."

"Finally, you're being sensible! I'll start packing right now."

"Good one. Yeah, good one officer." He forces a grin. "You really have a courageous sense of humour."

"Hello! I'm Gary. Very generous of you to help us out, officer."
"Hello, officer! Name's Gary. Boy, am I ever so grateful to you! But I'm not the only one who wants to thank you..." He nods toward Lena.
"Hey man..." he spreads his arms wide. "No one likes to hear it, but I'm not here to give you a false sense of security. It is what it is. People are starting to wake up and take notice."
"Hey, don't blame me, officer." He puts his hands up. "These are barbaric people and barbaric times we're talking about. Dark magic."
"Hey, man." He blushes. "All I meant was there are not many Seolites around here. I'm just stating a fact."
"Hey, you asked me, officer." He puts his hands up. "These are barbaric people and barbaric times we're talking about. Dark magic."
"How do you mean? Forgive me, officer, but we've only just met."
"How...?" The colour drains from his face.
"I always thought it was the Union, but... I sure as hell won't go around saying that anymore. You have my word. I don't know -- and I won't be running my mouth on this subject anymore."
"I always thought it was the Union... some Union hard-asses. Lynched him because of the strike. But almost everyone in town knows that. I wish I could tell you more..." He shakes his head.
"I can tell you it isn't something easy and immediately obvious, that's for sure. No way, that would be too easy..."
"I don't know officer... I think Future-Revachol might also have a few aces up its own sleeve. The people are starting to wake up, you see."
"I don't know what got *into* me. Stuffing my garbage in another man's property, it's... I've been having trouble at work lately. The Kojkos are price dumping us out of competition."
"I don't know what got into me, really... work has been stressful lately. Damn Kojkos price dumping us out of competition."

"I don't know who that is..." He blushes. "But all I meant was there are not many Seolites around here."

"I don't know... Sounds a bit *incestuous* to me, but sure -- none of my business, I'm not a Seolite." He quickly glances at the lieutenant. "But no way *that's* the reason they're winning the race..."
"I don't mean to sound paranoid or anything, *but*..."
"I don't pray, officer. Faith in non-existent helpers is a sign of weakness. Not for proper Revacholian men such as ourselves."
"I haven't really heard of any time-travel pills, officer..." He rubs his chin, thinking.
"I haven't the slightest. There's lots of weird stuff out here in the reeds, though -- insects, trash. Could be the wind shifting some garbage nearby."
"I hope I could help your investigation, in my small way." He's visibly relieved it's over.
"I just didn't want to bore you with unnecessary detail, officer."
"I knew you'd figure it out, officer." He sighs heavily. "I'm sorry I didn't tell you at once. I was..." He unbuttons the shirt.
"I know a guy who works with trash collection services -- CS Municipal. He gave me a master key for the trash containers of Martinaise."
"I know."
"I like nature, just not this bloody coast. It's mostly drunks and degenerates that come here."
"I like to pronounce it the *hard* way. The old way. The Vespertine way." He nods solemnly.
"I may have had a similar-looking mug in the past, that's all."
"I mean…" He turns toward Kim. "Officers."
"I once heard a story about a whole village disappearing overnight, without a trace. Can you imagine that?" He shakes his head. "Just a large patch of mud where the settlement was."
"I really owe you one for getting us out of those reeds, officer. Finally got all that soot out of my hair. Name's Gary."
"I thought you'd forgotten! I happen to have one on me right now." He smiles broadly as he walks behind the bar and takes a large, flat box out of a black bag. "It should still be warm."
"I told you everything -- I just took the cuirass that's all. I promise. I don't know anything else."
"I told you everything I know, sir. I'm *truly* sorry for the mug, but I have nothing to do with that." He shifts uncomfortably in his clothes.
"I took the hanged man's cuirass. I... I didn't mean to."
"I was ashamed of what I did. And I didn't want you to know." You see gleaming white ceramic shine underneath -- a thin layer of interlocking plates covers his gaunt torso.
"I was only cleaning up. I live right across the yard from where he was hanged and I saw him stripped naked. All the clothes lying around in the yard, smelling... People are animals, you know..."
"I was probably talking too loud in the Whirling the other night, about some theories... Stupid... Shouldn't have run my mouth loud like that."
"I was saying -- even as Seol remains closed off from the world, Seolite agents have been slowly advancing through the echelons of power on the other isolae."
"I won't cause any more trouble," he whispers. "I'll be Mr. Cooperation. The Union doesn't have to worry about me -- they're honest Vacholieres. Honest men."
"I won't do it again." He looks around nervously. "If there's anything I can do to assist you -- or the Union -- just ask, okay? I'll try to help if I can."
"I work as a special courier. You know, urgent deliveries, overnight deliveries, deliveries to out-of-the-way locations."
"I'd take a bullet for you, but I won't spend another hour out here."
"I'll explain later..." He doesn't muster up the strength to yell.
"I'm doing all I can in this economy, officer."

"I'm getting there, officer." He smiles. "You see, the Semper Maa has also evolved a curious defensive mechanism. When threatened, it has the ability to revert back to an earlier stage in its own lifecycle. It may even be able to do this *continually*, ad infinitum..."

"I'm getting there. See, the practice is derived from Semenese finger counting. Each segment of the finger represents one hour, so they count up to 12 with one hand, disregarding the thumb, of course."
"I'm just saying, as a *Revacholian*, I am slightly worried."
"I'm just waiting for my friend Morell to finish up with his insect traps so we can return to civilization."
"I'm not saying that *you* think that too. You seem like an incisive man, officer. You must be, being a detective."
"I'm so fucking sorry I called you *Yellow Man*." He says silently. "Seolite officers commanded the Suzerain's navy. Most of them sided with the King, when..." He shakes his head.
"I'm so fucking sorry I kept calling you *yellow man* in my head." He says silently. "Seolite officers commanded the Suzerain's navy. Most of them sided with the King, when..." He shakes his head.

"I'm sorry, okay? I thought I could cut costs. I shouldn't have. I shouldn't have disgraced myself."

"In the meantime, keep an eye on that partner of yours..." He lets the silence linger, then concludes: "Good talk."
"Is this about... the Union? Did the big man open the door?"
"Isn't it obvious? *Someone's* been feeding them a little trickle of tech down from someplace *no-one* else can reach..."

"It's a shame, too. What would we all do without law enforcement. But, as I was saying..."

"It's not like I go to meetings or anything."
"It's true that every expedition up to now has failed, and that several have *vanished* without a trace, but the potential is there, officer. It just can't be denied..."

"Lena, I'm sorry, but you're not *getting* anywhere, it was some kids. I know the little mutants around here -- leave anything out in the open and they'll steal it. Even if it's bugs." He looks at his tea.
"Like clockwork, I'm sure, no doubt about it. But is that *really* enough to take such an astronomical lead? I don't think so..."
"Listen, officer. I know it sounds like quite the task, but the potential, it just can't be denied..."
"Listen, there's no problem, officer. There's still the Semper Maa to consider, as well as this advanced Seolite technology."
"Local peasants call it the Passion Ring. They fear the rhinos. As, perhaps, they should. Anyway..."
"Lots of people out there miss the good old days."

"No-no..." He laughs nervously. "There's a discrepancy between how these Semenese tribes count and how they tell time."

"Of course. Of course."

"Officer," he says with confidence, "the average consumer is a moron. Leave it to them and we'd all be living in fake-bamboo huts, burning carcinogenic incense and playing the bongos. No way that's the reason!"

"Oh, this and that." He grins.
"Oh, uh... I didn't mean it in any *scientific* way." His gaze shifts nervously to the floor tiles.

"Oh, you know like... uhm..." He exhales loudly and continues to massage his neck. "Stealth aerostatics, blaasma-powered weaponry, all kinds of deep-secret projects..."
"Oh..." He looks surprised. "Well, I suppose there's still the deep-secret Seolite technology to consider."

"Okay, I work as a special courier." He smiles. "You know, urgent deliveries, overnight deliveries, deliveries to out-of-the-way locations."
"Okay, but... I told you everything. What else can I say?"

"Pale-related..." he repeats and pauses to think. "An interesting idea, but I can't say anything really comes to mind, no."
"People are just scared of the truth."

"So I can use the Whirling's trash compactor to store my own stuff," he says, bowing shamefully like a fallen knight. "Garbage disposal is expensive as hell, the damn Himeans run it like a mob..."

"Sometimes."

"Sure. If you want, I could get you one for free if we ever meet in the city, officer. Wheat free. Just ask me later."
"Sure. If you want, I could hook you up with some topping pie no problem."
"THEY'RE A *NASCENT CULTURE*. I just didn't feel comfortable, and... Let's change the topic, okay? Talk about your critters or whatever..." He mumbles something.
"Terrifying, right?" He scowls. "But we've gotta keep doing the good work, officer. One day, when we're stronger..."
"Thanks," the man mutters in the distance. He doesn't dare say more.

"That creates a loop, right? The more advanced tech they send here, the more advanced they become in the future, which means that by smuggling ever more advanced tech down to the past... I'm sure you can see where this is heading."

"The blue...? No, *the future*. The Seolites are helping themselves from the future. And every little incremental improvement they receive in the present has *major* ripples all along the timeline..."
"The flames are not just for decoration. They are an integral part of the beast's mating behaviour."
"The really sick bit is that they bite off bits of their *children's* fingers too. Even babies." He frowns. "Imagine that."
"The rhino starts running very fast to build heat, then stops, raises its head -- and sparks fly from its neck, setting its back ablaze."
"Then I came out to clean up the rags because *no one else would*. I put them into the Whirling's trash -- along with a broken mug, admittedly..." He changes his mind mid-sentence.
"There is no need, officer, I won't do it again. Besides, my pay, it's... I'm barely getting by as it is with those Kojkos edging on the delivery business, sir. Please..."
"There's lots of weird stuff out here in the reeds, though -- insects, trash. Could be the wind shifting some garbage nearby."
"They come as apparently well-meaning immigrants. Sometimes students -- they learn our *violin* and *cello*. But more often tech workers in cybernetics and similar advanced industries."
"They have special ducts just above their shoulder blades that secrete a combustible fluid. When the rhino is just beginning to light itself, it looks as though it has wings of fire."
"They play their violin and cello -- oh, we like your music! -- or work in unrelated fields, like, say, law enforcement, where they have access to a *lot* of sensitive data..."

"Those people were on a different rung of the ladder of civilization, that's all."
